content.value: HBCC has been bringing organised chess to Hobsons Bay since
1974 and has been affiliated with Chess Victoria since 1975
HBCC is formed in Altona North
Nissen huts at the Altona North Football Club
HBCC began when Kevin Brown and Bob Grieves (with early members including John Vranes and John Dunlop) played late into the night in the old football club changing huts — tough winters, huge passion.
Geoff Page became the first HBCC club champion — an early marker of the competitive culture forming around the club.
Move to Fifth Ave & first chess sets funded
A stronger home base in the western suburbs
As the sports club established at Fifth Ave, chess became part of the club (“why not chess?”). Max Fry donated $100 to buy sets, helping the club grow.
Bob Grieves and Kevin Brown famously played chess while being towed on a trailer in the street parade — sparking a long-running festival presence and many new members.
[bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”]
George Cagalj won the club championship three times (1978, 1980, 1981), with John Gedeljovski interrupting the run in 1979.
Peter Caissa took over as champion in 1982–84 (with Harry Schultheiss), reflecting the club’s growing strength and depth.
The inaugural Best in the West Open started a tradition of attracting top local and international players to Melbourne’s west — becoming a major name in Australian chess.
[bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”]
1985–1994: Big Names & Chess on the Air
Harry Schultheiss held the club championship through the mid-80s before the next wave of champions emerged.
A new contender arrives: Stan Christodoulou
Mario Zoppi commanded the late 80s. Around this time, Stan Christodoulou (Greek-Egyptian Candidate Master from Switzerland) joined the club.
First radio chess program in Australia
Club leaders helped launch “Chess Chat” on Stereo 974 — a dedicated chess community radio program that reached players across Melbourne via talkback and guests.
Featured in German chess magazine “Europa Rochade”
Chess Chat’s impact was recognised internationally when highlighted in “Europa Rochade.”
[bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”]
After the demise of ANBY Sports Club
With ANBY ending, the club moved through a series of venues across Altona and Williamstown — a challenging period of constant relocation.
Reborn as Hobsons Bay Chess Club
Move to ADASS Centre, Walker Close
The committee pushed for stability, and the club adopted the Hobsons Bay Chess Club name, relocating to the ADASS Centre near the club’s earliest origins.
In early 2003, the club moved to Joan Kirner House (refurbished former courthouse), continuing the search for the “right” long-term venue.
A stable home for larger events
By the end of 2003, Williamstown RSL became the home of chess in the western suburbs. Miles Patterson won the title during this transition.
[bold_timeline_item_button title=”Expand” style=”” shape=”” color=”” size=”inline” url=”#” el_class=”bold_timeline_group_button”]

we run and how ratings work.
Longer games (for example 60-90 minutes per player) played over several weeks as part of a club championship
Faster games (for example 10-25 minutes per player), often played as one-day or evening events, ideal for busy
After each round you're paired against someone on a similar score. You're not knocked out ? everyone keeps

We use ratings (club, ACF or FIDE, depending on the event) to help match players fairly and track improvement over time. Links to pairings and standings are usually shared via Tornelo or our tournament pages.

content.value: Getting started at HBCC is simple. Follow these steps and we’ll take care of the rest.
Decide whether you want to start with a social night (no clocks) or jump straight into a club tournament.
For most tournaments and social nights, you’ll register via our Member & Events portal – links are provided on our Calendar and event pages. If you’re unsure, send us a quick message.
Step 3 - Come Along a Bit Early
Arrive 10-15 minutes before the start time so we can say hello, show you around and answer any questions.
Just bring yourself and a positive attitude. We provide boards, pieces and clocks. If you know how to keep score, bring a pen.
Not sure where to start? Contact us and we’ll recommend the best first session for you.

fields.title: Do I need to be a member to play?

content.value: You can often try a session or event before committing to membership, but regular players will be asked to join HBCC.

fields.title: I haven't played in years is that OK?

content.value: Absolutely. Many of our adult players are returning to chess after a long break.

fields.title: Do I need to know how to use a chess clock and keep score?

content.value: It helps for tournaments, but we’re happy to show you. Social nights are a great place to learn without pressure.

fields.title: Are there minimum age requirements for club nights?

content.value: Younger juniors usually start in our Juniors program. Older juniors who are comfortable with clocks may be invited into seniors events – speak with our coaches or committee.
Event and membership fees are kept affordable. Please see our Membership page for current rates.
Join us for a social night or club event and discover why HBCC is the home of chess in Melbourne’s West.

fields.alt: Chess at Hobsons Bay Chess Club

content.value: Over the history of the Hobsons Bay Chess Club, dating back to 1974, there are many people whose contribution we cherish and all would agree that the person with the greatest impact over these years was Peter Caissa. Peter was a long-standing president and junior coach of the club and also a friend and mentor to its members.

Sadly, he lost his battle with cancer in 2012. Peterâ€™s contribution to the club goes beyond that of the positions he held. His love of chess was strong, so much so, he changed his surname to Caissa by deed poll. To those that knew him, played with and against him, his passion for the game was infectious
The legacy of Peterâ€™s commitment to junior chess and coaching remain strong today.

Many now adult players at the club gained the love of the game through Peterâ€™s dedication and owe much to his hard work. Peter said some of his proudest moments was seeing juniors at the club mature by playing chess. Peter was also the driving force behind the annual Best in the West weekend tournament, bringing some of Victoriaâ€™s best chess talent together, along with interstate and international players. The Best in the West tournament had become the biggest chess event in Melbourneâ€™s
west and is still going strong today.

Away from the Hobsons Bay Chess Club, Peter had terrific success in international correspondence chess events, winning and captaining a number of International Correspondence Federation events. In the 1990s, he helped bring chess to the Melbourne airways through the weekly â€œChess Chatâ€ program. These involvements elevated Peter as a much loved member of the Australian chess community.
In 2012, the Hobsons Bay Chess Club took the decision to honour Peter by awarding the Peter Caissa Cup to the winner of the annual club championship.

To win the Peter Caissa Cup is no small achievement. Firstly, it requires players to qualify as one of the top eight players during regular season play. The winner is then required to outperform the other seven qualifiers in a round robin club championship event.
The words below are a tribute to Peter written by Dallas Gatti, a long time club
member and inaugural winner of the Peter Caissa cup.

fields.title: wp-page-5021-section-1: Chess at Hobsons Bay Chess Club
fields.alt: Chess at Hobsons Bay Chess Club

content.value: Winning the inaugural Peter Caissa was for me, a huge honour. Peter had not been at the club for quite a while due to his health, but he had planned on being there on presentation night to hand over the cup that was named in his honour. I was looking forward to receive the cup from him, my friend. But the news broke that night, that was not going to happen. I didn’t make a speech that night, my emotions got the better of me.

I met Peter Caissa in around 1988, when the club had organised a simul at the Altona Festival. Peter was my first point of contact with the club, and was the first point of contact for many members who joined the club before and after myself. Peter was a great character and stalwart of the club. He would be one of the first people there to help start setting the club up, and one of the last to leave at the end of the evening. He wore many hats, from taking photos and submitting them to local papers to try to increase the clubs recognition, club president, tournament director, arbiter, Winter Inter-club team organiser, and even help organise a chess radio program on local radio. Everything he did, for the club, he did with passion and selflessness.

He was a great ambassador for the club. But not only that, he was a great person in life. He was a true friend to most people, and would help you out however he could. Simply, thank you Peter for all that you have done for myself personally during my difficult times in life, and I hope wherever you are, you stop playing the French Defence!!

fields.title: Record turnout for women's chess in Altona
fields.excerpt: Star Weekly reports on 42 players at the Victorian Women's Championship and the growing participation of women and girls.
fields.imageAlt: A championship participant holds her trophy beside a club representative at the HBCC awards presentation.

content.value: HBCC shared Star Weekly's coverage of the 2026 Victorian Women's Championship, held in Altona on 12 and 19 September.
The newspaper reported a field of 42 players, up 40 per cent from 2025. Deethya Sai Katakam and Narelle Szuveges shared first place.
The report also highlighted the participation of junior girls and the live broadcast of games. Read the original story for the full report.
Club photograph from HBCC's championship album. Championship figures and results are attributed to Star Weekly.

content.value: Hobsons Bay Chess Club has shared its photo gallery from the 2026 Victorian Women's Championship and awards presentation.
HBCC and Geelong Chess Club co-organised the event under Chess Victoria. The club thanked Melissa Horne MP for presenting awards to the participants.
